title: Otter.ai raises $320 million from General Catalyst’s growth fund for its meeting tool
slides: Why does a meeting tool need $320 million?
General Catalyst's growth fund led the round.
Otter now sells AI agents that attend meetings for you.
Teams may soon skip live calls entirely.
Check what Otter's agents record before adopting them.
thread_text:
1. $320M for a meeting tool?

Otter just raised that much to build AI agents that join calls in your place. The company bets you will pay to skip live meetings entirely.

2. Growth fund leads the round

General Catalyst's growth fund led the investment, signaling that major backers see AI meeting agents as a real business, not a feature.

3. Agents attend so you don't

Otter now sells AI agents that join your meetings, take notes, and report back. The pitch: send the agent, skip the call, and get a summary instead.

4. The end of live calls?

If agents can represent you well enough, teams may stop scheduling live calls altogether. That changes how work gets done, not just how meetings are recorded.

5. Check what they record first

Before you adopt Otter's agents, ask what they capture and who can access it. Take one real meeting this week and test the agent's output before trusting it.

instagram.caption:
Someone just raised $320 million so AI can sit in meetings instead of you. 🎥

Otter.ai's agents join your calls, take notes, and report back. General Catalyst's growth fund led the round, betting this is a real business, not a feature.

The pitch: send the agent, skip the call, get a summary. If it works, teams may stop scheduling live meetings at all.

For anyone who runs meetings or publishes content from them, that shifts the work from showing up to checking output.

One catch before you try it: ask what the agent records and who can access it. 📋

Would you let an AI attend a client call in your place? 🤔
